verses.text: You are righteous, Yahweh, when I contend with you; yet I would reason the cause with you: why does the way of the wicked prosper? why are all they at ease who deal very treacherously?
You have planted them, yes, they have taken root; they grow, yes, they produce fruit. You are near in their mouth, and far from their heart.
But you, Yahweh, know me; you see me, and try my heart toward you. Pull them out like sheep for the slaughter, and prepare them for the day of slaughter.

How long shall the land mourn, and the herbs of the whole country wither? For the wickedness of those who dwell therein, the animals are consumed, and the birds; because they said, “He shall not see our latter end.”
“If you have run with the footmen, and they have wearied you, then how can you contend with horses? Though in a land of peace you are secure, yet how will you do in the pride of the Jordan?
For even your brothers, and the house of your father, even they have dealt treacherously with you; even they have cried aloud after you! Don’t believe them, though they speak beautiful words to you.
“I have forsaken my house. I have cast off my heritage. I have given the dearly beloved of my soul into the hand of her enemies.
My heritage has become to me as a lion in the forest. She has uttered her voice against me; therefore I have hated her.
Is my heritage to me as a speckled bird of prey? Are the birds of prey against her all around? Go, assemble all the animals of the field, bring them to devour.
Many shepherds have destroyed my vineyard. They have trodden my portion under foot. They have made my pleasant portion a desolate wilderness.
They have made it a desolation. It mourns to me, being desolate. The whole land is made desolate, because no man lays it to heart.
Destroyers have come on all the bare heights in the wilderness; for the sword of Yahweh devours from the one end of the land even to the other end of the land. No flesh has peace.
They have sown wheat, and have reaped thorns. They have put themselves to pain, and profit nothing. You shall be ashamed of your fruits, because of the fierce anger of Yahweh.”

Yahweh says, “Concerning all my evil neighbors, who touch the inheritance which I have caused my people Israel to inherit: behold, I will pluck them up from off their land, and will pluck up the house of Judah from among them.
It shall happen, after that I have plucked them up, I will return and have compassion on them; and I will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.

It shall happen, if they will diligently learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, ‘As Yahweh lives;’ even as they taught my people to swear by Baal; then shall they be built up in the middle of my people.
But if they will not hear, then I will pluck up that nation, plucking up and destroying it,” says Yahweh.

footnotes.content: Jeremiah brings his complaint straight to the Lord—not in defiance but in honest wrestling. He sees the wicked prosper and knows God is righteous, so he asks the deepest question: why? This is the prayer of a man who trusts God enough to speak what troubles him most.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here is the prophet's real burden: they have God's name on their lips but not His love in their hearts. I've watched this too—people who know all the right words but live as though the Lord doesn't see their deeds. God knows the difference between the mouth and the heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah appeals to what only God knows—the Lord 'tries' his heart (tests it, proves it true). He asks God to separate him from the false, as a shepherd pulls lambs for safekeeping before judgment comes. This is the cry of someone proven and clinging to it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land itself groans under the weight of human wickedness. Even the animals and birds suffer for the pride of those who deny God's judgment. Jeremiah sees that sin is never private—it spreads outward, touching the whole creation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's answer comes not with comfort but with a hard question: How can you complain now if you'll stumble when the trial grows fiercer? The Jordan's 'pride' speaks of swelling floods—worse is coming, and Jeremiah must prepare himself in spirit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophet's own family has turned against him—a specific wound that echoes throughout his ministry. Even when they speak fair words, he is told not to trust them. This loneliness is part of what God asks him to bear as His messenger.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now God Himself speaks His grief. To hear the Lord say 'I have forsaken my house' is to understand the depth of Judah's rebellion and the pain it costs the Father. He has given over what He held most dear because they would not turn back.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's own possession has become hostile to Him—like a wild lion that roars against its owner. This is the sorrow of love spurned and trust broken. Even the Lord's chosen people have turned their face from Him and drawn His hatred against their own faithlessness.
footnotes.author: LJT Insight

footnotes.content: God's heritage is prey now, marked and vulnerable, surrounded by enemies. The image is savage: birds of prey circling, all the wild beasts called to feed on what was meant to be protected. This is what abandonment looks like when a people turn from their God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The 'shepherds' here are false leaders who destroyed what they were meant to tend. They have trampled God's vineyard into a wasteland. When those who lead turn away from the Lord, they leave the people defenseless before judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The desolation spreads because 'no man lays it to heart'—nobody stops to grieve, to repent, to turn back. A land mourning without a people mourning with it is a land without hope. But grief itself would be a step toward restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord's sword ranges across the whole land—no shelter, no peace anywhere. When judgment sweeps through, no flesh escapes. This is what the prophet has been warning them about, and now the reality of it unfolds in every direction.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They have sown wheat, the good seed, yet reaped only thorns. Their labor has come to nothing; their shame is complete. This is what happens when people work against God's way—all their effort becomes a mockery of intention.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God now turns His word toward the 'evil neighbors' who touch Israel's inheritance—Judah will not stand alone in judgment. The Lord is sovereign over all nations and will uproot those who threaten His people, even as He uproots Judah itself for her sin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After the plucking up comes the tender word: compassion and return. Each person restored to their own land and heritage—this is the promise hidden in judgment itself. God's justice always moves toward restoration if hearts will turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the nations can be woven into God's people if they learn His ways and swear by His name alone. This is grace extended: they who once taught Israel to swear by Baal can be rebuilt in the midst of Israel if they will truly turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in these words: refusal to hear brings uprooting and destruction. As of 2026-10, I see how often the invitation to learn God's ways still stands before us, and the consequence of hardened ears remains just as sure. The choice remains ours.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
